India imported a record-high level of crude oil volumes in October, trade data showed on Thursday, as volumes from Saudi Arabia jumped to an eight-month high amid a recovery in Gulf shipments.

India imported a record 5.58 million barrels per day (bpd) of crude oil last month, up by 4.7% compared to September and a 6.9% rise from October 2025, according to the trade data cited by Reuters.

Russia remained the single largest oil supplier to India, with Indian imports rising by 3.5% in October compared to September. At 1.85 million bpd, India’s crude oil imports from Russia accounted for about one-third of total purchases.

Russia remains a key crude oil supplier to India, but the rebound in Hormuz flows and the shorter distance to India have boosted Indian imports of crude oil from the Gulf producers.

Saudi Arabia significantly raised its shipments to India, to an eight-month high of 790,000 bpd in October, according to the trade data. The Kingdom thus toppled the United Arab Emirates (UAE) from the second spot of India’s top oil suppliers. Indian oil imports from the UAE slumped to 612,000 bpd in October, a seven-month low.

So Russia remained the biggest oil supplier to India in October, followed by Saudi Arabia, which overtook the UAE for the first time since the war began.

The Saudis, apart from boosting exports, offered discounts for their crude grades to offset higher shipping costs, beating the other Middle Eastern producers on pricing, refining sources in India told Reuters.

At the end of October, Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL), one of the biggest Indian state-owned refiners, said it would reduce its purchases of crude oil from Russia in November as high freight costs and premiums for Russia’s crude undermine the attractiveness of Moscow’s oil compared to multiple offers for Middle Eastern crude, whose prices are falling.
